predecessors.name: Southern Han
predecessors.text: northern Vietnam, which 'was militarily occupied by the Southern Han' before Ngô Quyền's dynasty (Ngô dynasty page; 'Third Era of Northern Domination')

successors.name: Ming dynasty
successors.text: the Hồ state's land, conquered by the Ming in 1407 (Hồ dynasty page: 'The Hồ dynasty was conquered by the Chinese Ming dynasty in 1407'); Cliopatria's Ming shape grows by about 133,000 km2 in 1407

ledger.x: 939: Ngô Quyền founds the Ngô dynasty at Cổ Loa, ending Southern Han rule.
968: Đinh Bộ Lĩnh ends the Anarchy of the 12 Warlords and founds Đại Cồ Việt at Hoa Lư.
968: the capital moves from Cổ Loa to Hoa Lư.
980: Lê Hoàn takes the throne after the murder of Đinh Bộ Lĩnh (October 979); the Anterior Lê rule Đại Cồ Việt (infobox 980-1009). Đinh page: 'General Lê Hoàn succeeded the throne: 980'.
982: Lê Đại Hành's army sacks Indrapura and defeats Champa.
983: Champa becomes a vassal of Đại Cồ Việt.
989: the Vietnamese presence at Indrapura closes.
1009: Lý Công Uẩn is crowned and the Lý dynasty replaces the Anterior Lê.
1010: Lý Thái Tổ moves the capital from Hoa Lư to Thăng Long.
1054: Lý Thánh Tông changes the state name from Đại Cồ Việt to Đại Việt.
1069: Lý Thánh Tông takes three districts from Champa.
1069: Champa's first vassalage closes.
1075: Lý Thường Kiệt invades the Song.
1076: a Song army of over 300,000 invades Đại Việt.
1077: Lý Thường Kiệt stops the Song at the Như Nguyệt River and offers peace.
1077: the Song keep Quảng Nguyên.
1082: Đại Việt gives back Yong, Qin and Lian.
1082: the Song return Quảng Nguyên.
1132: Suryavarman II and the Cham briefly seize Nghệ An.
1136: a Vietnamese force under Đỗ Anh Vũ counterattacks across Laos and the Cham make peace.
1225: Trần Cảnh replaces the Lý.
1258: the Mongols under Uriyangkhadai take Thăng Long for nine days.
1258: the Mongols leave Thăng Long after nine days (the page gives no calendar date).
1285: the Yuan take Thăng Long.
9 June 1285: 'Mongol troops evacuated Thăng Long to withdraw to China' after the decisive Trần victory at Chương Dương.
February 1288: Toghon's Yuan army returns to Thăng Long.
1288: the Yuan 'retreated from Thăng Long to their fortified main base in Vạn Kiếp on 5 March 1288'; their fleet was destroyed at Bạch Đằng in April 1288.
1306: Chế Mân cedes Ô and Lý for Princess Huyền Trân.
1312: Trần Anh Tông defeats Champa and sets up its king.
1326: Champa wins back independence.
1363: the westernmost uplands leave the shape.
1371: Chế Bồng Nga's Cham raids begin.
1390: Trần Khát Chân kills Chế Bồng Nga.
1397: the court leaves Thăng Long for Thanh Hóa.
1400: Hồ Quý Ly deposes the Trần and founds the Hồ dynasty (Đại Ngu).
1402: Hồ Hán Thương's army forces Champa to cede 'large territory'.
1406: the land ceded in 1402 returns to Champa.
11 May 1406: the Ming invade.
1407: the Hồ are defeated.
1407: the Ming take all of Đại Ngu and rule it as the Fourth Era of Northern Domination (Jiaozhi).
1407: the Hồ dynasty falls to the Ming and Đại Việt is absorbed as the Ming province of Jiaozhi (infobox 'Disestablished: 1407', succeeded by the 'Fourth Era of Northern Domination').

wars.name: Song-Đại Cồ Việt war of 980-981
wars.outcome: The Song invasion ordered by Taizong in 980 was halted at Bạch Đằng in 981 and ended in peace talks; the Song accepted Lê Hoàn as military governor.

wars.name: Lê Hoàn's invasion of Champa
wars.outcome: Indrapura sacked and the Cham king killed in 982; the new king agreed to be a vassal in 983.

wars.name: Lý Thánh Tông's invasion of Champa
wars.outcome: Rudravarman III captured; Địa Lí, Ma Linh and Bố Chính ceded and the tributary system restored.

wars.name: Suryavarman II's wars against Đại Việt
wars.outcome: A Khmer army of 20,000 was routed at Nghệ An in 1128; with Cham help the Khmer briefly took Nghệ An in 1132; a Vietnamese counterattack in 1136 and the Cham peace ended the effort; no land changed hands.

wars.name: Lý-Song War
wars.outcome: Lý forces took Qinzhou, Lianzhou and Yongzhou (1075-1076); the Song invasion of 1076-77 was stopped at the Như Nguyệt River; the Song kept Quảng Nguyên until a 1082 exchange returned it for the three prefectures; the 1084 talks fixed the frontier.

wars.name: First Mongol invasion of Đại Việt
wars.outcome: The Mongols took Thăng Long and left after nine days; Trần Thái Tông returned and a tributary relationship began.

wars.name: Second Mongol invasion of Đại Việt
wars.outcome: Toghon crossed on 27 January, took Thăng Long in late February and withdrew on 9 June 1285; Sogetu's column came up through Nghệ An.

wars.name: Third Mongol invasion of Đại Việt
wars.outcome: The Yuan occupied Thăng Long in February 1288, withdrew to Vạn Kiếp on 5 March and lost their fleet at Bạch Đằng in April; both Đại Việt and Champa accepted nominal Yuan supremacy.

wars.name: Trần campaign against Champa of 1312
wars.outcome: Three Vietnamese columns defeated and captured Chế Chí; Anh Tông installed a successor; relations 'remained strained'.

wars.name: Champa-Đại Việt War (1367-1390)
wars.outcome: Chế Bồng Nga sacked Thăng Long in 1371, 1377, 1378 and 1383; a 1376 Vietnamese campaign was beaten at Đồ Bàn; Chế Bồng Nga was killed in the first lunar month of 1390.

wars.name: Hồ invasion of Champa of 1402
wars.outcome: Champa ceded large territory to Đại Ngu.

wars.name: Ming conquest of Đại Ngu
wars.outcome: The Ming invaded on 11 May 1406 and conquered the Hồ in 1407.

certainty.note: Delta and Thanh-Nghệ are firm; the uplands to the Chinese frontier and the Champa march are claimed, not surveyed.

The Quảng Nguyên-Guihua frontier fixed in the 1084 talks 'exists largely unmodified to the present day' and is the one sharp border; the Champa frontier (Hải Vân line from 1306) and the western uplands are approximate.
